transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-13 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Kai (Redwood CSM), Alicia (Skyward Head of AI), Marcus (CTO), Priya (Solutions Architect), Ethan (Sales)

Summary: Quick co-sell / pipeline review. Samira opens with pipeline status; Jordan covers technical asks; Priya drives infra constraints. Natural crosstalk and some transcription oddities (Redwood Dedicate, K V cash, etc.).

00:00:05 - Samira Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call
Samira here from Redwood, Jordan our SE, Kai from CS. How's everyone at Skyward?
00:00:12 - Alicia Wong: Hi Samira, Alicia here, Marcus and Priya on the line too. Ethan also. Thanks for organizing.
00:00:20 - Samira Patel: Great. The agenda
co-sell pipeline, three priority deals, any blockers, and technical follow-ups. We'll keep it pretty tight so we can get to the deep dive items.
00:00:35 - Marcus Diaz: Sounds good. We're super interested in the pilot with the recommendation engine, curious about latency and cost tradeoffs.
00:00:45 - Jordan Lee: Cool, on the pilot
are you leaning hosted or private? I know you mentioned VPC peering last time.
00:00:51 - Priya Mehta: Yes, we're evaluating. For the pilot we'd like hosted for speed, but enterprise is definitely private/VPC later; we have strict network egress policies, so the private deployment is the real ask.
00:01:05 - Kai Thompson: Noted. We usually recommend starting hosted to iterate fast, then migrate a pinned model to Dedicated or Private as needed.
00:01:12 - Ethan Cole: From a sales standpoint, faster time to demo helps conversion, so hosted pilot is appealing. But legal/security will push private for enterprise.
00:01:25 - Samira Patel: Great — that aligns with the joint motion: fast hosted pilot -> Dedicated reserved capacity for scale -> Private/VPC for enterprise. We'll include co-sell pricing scenarios in the doc.

00:05:10 - Jordan Lee: Tech notes
one of the things to surface: we can do prefix caching and batching to cut per-token costs, but that affects latency sometimes. For recommendation workloads with short context, batching helps a lot.
00:05:28 - Priya Mehta: Can you quantify? Right now our 95th percentile latency needs to be under 250ms per request for the web use case.
00:05:36 - Jordan Lee: With a dedicated pool and optimized kernels, we typically hit 120
180ms for 512 tokens, but it's workload dependent. If you need strict p95 under 250ms we can tune batching and KV cache; also quantization plays a role.
00:05:54 - Marcus Diaz: When you say quantization, are you talking like 4-bit? Any impact on model quality for our ranking model?
00:06:03 - Jordan Lee: Yeah, we've seen 4-bit quant performs well for many transformer models; for ranking you might see a small delta. We'll recommend a short eval against your test set.

00:10:02 - Alicia Wong: Security
SOC2, SSO, KMS. We need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed keys and audit logs for Private.
00:10:12 - Samira Patel: Yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. For Dedicated we can enable KMS too; hosted supports encryption at rest, and you can bring-your-own-key in some enterprise plans. We'll send the security pack.
00:10:30 - Priya Mehta: Also need clarity on data residency and retention - we have EU customers so region pinning is important.
00:10:38 - Kai Thompson: We can pin regions; our private control plane supports region restrictions. We'll include a short doc with retention settings.

00:15:40 - Ethan Cole: Pipeline review
three deals: 1) Pilot (mid-market financial startup) 
 exec sponsor, decision in 6 weeks; 2) Expansion (existing customer upsell) 
 procurement loop, legal questions around log retention; 3) Enterprise prospect (large retail chain) 
 requires VPC, SOC2, and onsite audit.
00:15:55 - Samira Patel: Good 
 which one is the top priority for joint marketing / proof points?
00:16:01 - Alicia Wong: The enterprise prospect is biggest ARR but longest cycle. Pilot is where we can win fast for a co-sell win.
00:16:09 - Samira Patel: Agreed. We'll focus co-sell resources on the pilot to get a fast win, and parallelize security docs for enterprise.

00:22:05 - Priya Mehta: On VPC peering
our infra team requires that the inference endpoints live on private subnets with no public egress; can Redwood support air-gapped or on-prem later?
00:22:18 - Jordan Lee: Yes, our Private deployment can be on-prem or VPC-only with no public egress. There are some deployment ops considerations 
 we'll need an infra diagram and a list of required ports.
00:22:30 - Priya Mehta: Okay we'll send the diagram. Also, what's the control plane model 
 do you run a managed control plane in the customer's VPC or a customer-managed control plane?
00:22:38 - Samira Patel: For Private we offer both: managed control plane in the customer's VPC (customer-managed networking) or an on-prem package for air-gapped. We'll outline the support matrix in the security pack.

00:30:12 - Marcus Diaz: Performance benchmarks 
 we want to run a 48-hour soak test and 95th percentile latency benchmarks. What telemetry do you expose?
00:30:22 - Jordan Lee: Redwood Console exposes per-route latency, token breakdown, trace hooks, and error rates. For Dedicated/Private we can give more granular tracing and access to raw logs per request. We'll propose a benchmark plan and collect sample payloads.
00:30:38 - Priya Mehta: We'll provide top-5 query patterns and expected QPS.

00:38:00 - Ethan Cole: Objections we typically hear 
 pricing transparency vs unit economics. How do we present hosted vs dedicated costs to procurement?
00:38:11 - Samira Patel: We'll send a straightforward cost model: per-token hosted price, reserved capacity committed monthly for Dedicated with discount tiers, and a licensing + infra ops estimate for Private. Include examples based on your QPS and token distribution.
00:38:28 - Alicia Wong: Competitors
Anthropic and OpenAI are in the conversation. We need to understand where Redwood's sweet spot is.
00:38:36 - Samira Patel: Redwood positions on production economics 
 predictable latency, cost controls (batching, cache, quantization), and unified tooling across modes. We'll share a one-pager comparing the three for common infra patterns.

00:45:50 - Jordan Lee: Quick note
model variants and fallback policies: we can route to cheaper quantized variants on overload and fall back to higher-quality hosted models if needed. Useful for graceful degradation during peaks.
00:46:02 - Marcus Diaz: That sounds promising as a reliability feature. How does that affect auditability?
00:46:08 - Kai Thompson: All routing decisions and rollouts are logged in the console. We'll include an example export.

00:52:15 - Samira Patel: Recap 
 Samira to share co-sell doc + pricing + security pack; Jordan runs benchmark plan and schedules technical deep dive; Priya sends infra diagram; Kai provisions demo access.
00:52:30 - Priya Mehta: We'll also send a short data retention and residency policy list.
00:52:36 - Samira Patel: Perfect. Any other questions?
00:52:42 - Alicia Wong: No, just please highlight any assumptions about custom model ingestion and tokenization costs.
00:52:49 - Jordan Lee: Will do 
 will add: model size, seq length, tokenization impact, and expected KV cache hit rates.
00:53:05 - Ethan Cole: From sales 
 we'll prep a joint talking points doc for the pilot.
00:53:12 - Samira Patel: Great, thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after the deep dive.
00:54:00 - (meeting ends, light crosstalk)

Notes on transcript quality: medium 
 occasional mis-ids (Redwood Dedicate / K V cash) and run-on sentences; speakers sometimes overlap.

References/Artifacts mentioned: co-sell one-pager (link to be shared), benchmark spreadsheet (customer to share), infra diagram (customer to share), security pack (Redwood to send).
